reason: A host shutdown that quiesced some projects and then aborted left their workers alive, closed and unowned with process rows still 'ready'. Auto-admission then skipped every new demand (any unowned execution process blocks it), and a stale pending entry re-claimed a released project onto its closed worker (claim committed before the worker refused the attach), so the heartbeat kept that project owned by a worker that could never run it. Releasing a quiesced project now drains its worker's process row in the same transaction, attach_execution claims only for an unassigned worker and refuses a bound worker that does not hold the current grant, the retirement reconciler also retires workers quiesced by an aborted host shutdown, and auto-admission drops a pending process that is no longer reserved, starting or ready. Selected suites cover quiescence with an aborted shutdown, the retirement reconciler, deployment status and lifecycle, the execution worker, automatic recovery, Work batch idle retirement and the recovery attach path.
exclusions: Process-level and LAN-fixture suites (test_runtime_reconciliation, test_runtime_integration_credentials, test_runtime_host_settings, test_runtime_host_operator, test_shutdown_readmission, most of test_recovery_reconciliation) fail locally with 24 identical cases on pristine main and on this branch, so they are not selected. No UI, native or Playwright cases: no frontend code changed. PostgreSQL variants run where NEBULA_TEST_POSTGRES_URL is set.
